summary.headline: Mufin Green Finance Q2 FY27 AUM rose 10.4% QoQ to ₹1,766 crore; H1 PAT about ₹29 crore, with Gross NPA down to 1.77%.
summary.overview: AUM reached ₹1,766 crore at September 30, 2026, up 10.4% QoQ and 71.8% YoY, with disbursements of ₹590 crore (up 31% QoQ). Mediclaim financing and Salary Saathi now make up about 44% of AUM, while climate finance fell from 29.8% to 19.1%. Profit before tax rose to ₹19.47 crore from ₹18.82 crore in Q1, while net interest income fell to ₹33.27 crore from ₹35 crore. Management says the company is pivoting from climate lending to digital lending, and it disclosed an RBI approval for an AD-II forex licence.

segments.name: Mediclaim financing (digital)
segments.commentary: AUM ₹686.90 crore, 38.9% of total; average ticket ~₹51,000, tenor 2-60 months, yields 18-24%, integrated with 10+ insurers. PTC rated 'A+' by CRISIL; DA deal with Credit Saison assessed at 1% ±0.25% LGD.

segments.name: Salary Saathi (digital)
segments.commentary: AUM ₹90.61 crore, 5.1% of total; personal loans to Rajasthan and Assam government employees, launched February 2026, disbursed within 1-2 hours via HRMS integration.

segments.name: Climate finance (EV/green)
segments.commentary: Share of AUM fell from 29.8% to 19.1%; management says new climate disbursements are now retail-only and tightly underwritten. Remaining book includes ~₹100-110 crore L3/L5 vehicle loans and ~₹60-70 crore battery loans, with ~₹25 crore of stated residual pain.

segments.name: Arthum (workforce/contract-worker financing)
segments.commentary: Company holds a 20% stake; launching now with one-month tenure products for contract workers, priced at ~3-5% per month via PPI-licensed wallet. Management cites a ₹20,000-30,000 crore monthly payout pool.

guidance_outlook: AUM projected at about ₹2,500 crore by end of FY27 (March 2027).
No fresh equity needed until AUM reaches roughly ₹3,000-3,500 crore; current equity plus accruals expected to support borrowings for the next two financial years.
Long-term ambition stated: annual PAT of ₹500 crore without equity dilution; management says FY28 will be a 'golden period' and that ~10% of the vision has been achieved this year.
Life insurance financing product expected to go live in about one month.
Operating headcount target of 300 for this year; currently 306 employees, down from ~500 in FY26.
capex_capacity: Technology spend is rising: servers migrated to AWS, SentinelOne deployed, quarterly external audits and empanelled VAPT audits, per management. Management called the infrastructure expensive but said it would scale with AUM. No amount disclosed.
Company is now a Middle Layer NBFC under RBI scale-based regulation, bringing new infrastructure and audit requirements.
RBI approved an Authorised Dealer Category II (AD-II) forex licence, obtained by direct application as an NBFC; official announcement pending.
Monthly disbursements for Arthum-type short-tenure products could reach ₹1,200-1,500 crore, per management's projection.
demand_pricing: Health insurance premiums grew 31% YoY per industry data; 40-45% of first-time buyers choose monthly payments, so management expects premium financing to grow 20-25% a year. GST on health insurance cut to zero.
Around 50 players are replicating Mediclaim financing; management says six have entered since launch (BimaPay). Management expects pricing competition rather than product competition.
Cost of funds is falling as PSU banks onboard (SBI, IOB, Union Bank, IDBI Bank); IDBI Bank and South Indian Bank were added in Q2. Cost of borrowing fell by over 100 bps over the past year.
Some lenders have been asked to reclassify new products as impact lending; about 25-30% have switched so far.
Interest expense grew 103.7% YoY because surplus liquidity is held to cover the next three to four months of EMIs.

qa_highlights.question: What is climate finance's share of AUM, why are new climate disbursements still happening, and how much pain is left?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said climate focus is now zero and only retail is being done under tighter policies. Residual pain is about ₹25 crore; the remaining book is ~₹100-110 crore L3/L5 vehicle loans, ~₹60-70 crore battery loans, and cars and buses. Lines from US DFC can only be deployed into electric mobility.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 1.77% Gross NPA and 1.50% Net NPA is from new versus legacy products?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said total NPA is about ₹30 crore, of which only about ₹1 crore is from the new book; the rest is from EV retail, and 99% of the EV NPA is from the old book, already provided for.

qa_highlights.question: How far can AUM grow on current net worth and accruals, and when is capital needed?
qa_highlights.answer: No fresh capital needed until ~₹3,000-3,500 crore AUM, likely FY28. Management said capital is not a constraint but dilution would be costly. Direct assignments are not being done merely to retire debt because borrowings must be serviced.

qa_highlights.question: What is being done on technology investment and cybersecurity as the company becomes more tech-enabled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said digital lenders face heightened cyber threat. It hired a CISO (Amit Sharma, ex-SBI Cards) and Harish Arora for information security, migrated servers to AWS, deployed SentinelOne, and runs quarterly audits. Management called the spend 'expensive' but said it will scale with AUM.

qa_highlights.question: What is the competitive moat as tech-based products are easy to replicate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the Arthum edge: one of only four PPI licences, a contractor-worker ERP partner, and in-house NBFC lending, which it said took six months to build versus a year to 1.5 years for others. For BimaPay, it said competition has become a pricing war.

qa_highlights.question: What is the AI strategy beyond underwriting?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI is not a key underwriting factor because lending is anchored on insurers or state-government repayment. AI is used in DevOps coding and multilingual collection bots. An analyst suggested adding an R&D and AI investment slide from next quarter; management was open to it.

risks_watch: Debt-to-equity rose to 2.89x from 2.43x; borrowings grew faster than net worth.
Management's ~4% ROA and ₹500 crore PAT aspirations are not yet supported by disclosed FY27 guidance; H1 PAT of ~₹29 crore is partly driven by a shift in mix.
Arthum launch (3-5% per month pricing, contract-worker lending) is new and unproven at scale; management said it will avoid collection-heavy lending.
Cybersecurity exposure is rising with digital growth; management acknowledged gaps that senior hires were brought in to address.
Residual EV/climate book (~₹25 crore stated pain) and the timing of the lender reclassification to impact lending.
Net interest income fell QoQ to ₹33.27 crore from ₹35 crore despite higher AUM; interest expense is elevated by liquidity held for EMIs.
Management stated that the BluSmart exposure and rickshaw book cost ₹15-25 crore in earlier periods; the impact on future quarters is not quantified.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on the digital pivot, ROA and the AD-II licence, with the MD speaking at length on long-term vision. Notably candid on past mistakes (climate lending, BluSmart, rickshaw book). Answers on AI and competition were specific, but there were few hard numbers on the cybersecurity spend and the Arthum economics.
key_quotes: We do not want to be an AUM-driven company; we want to be a profitability-driven company.
Still, we regret running climate financing for three years when its returns were nothing like what our new products are delivering. That was a mistake.
We will not need fresh capital until we reach approximately ₹3,000 to 3,500 crores of AUM.

growth.why: Management guides AUM of about ₹2,500 crore by March 2027 from ₹1,766 crore at Sep 30, 2026 (~42% rise in H2), backed by Q2 disbursements of ₹590 crore (+31% QoQ), new digital products and falling cost of funds, but no physical capacity, sanctioned orders or explicit capital plan were given beyond a qualitative disbursement projection.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Cost of borrowing fell over 100 bps and PSU banks are onboarding, but NII fell to ₹33.27 crore from ₹35 crore, interest expense rose 103.7% YoY from liquidity held for EMIs, and Mediclaim is facing pricing competition.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No physical capacity addition discussed; headcount is falling to a 300 target from 306 now, and the only adds are a life-insurance financing product and the Arthum trial launch, which are product rather than capacity moves.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: AUM rose 10.4% QoQ to ₹1,766 crore and disbursements rose 31% QoQ to ₹590 crore; health premiums grew 31% YoY and management expects premium financing to grow 20-25% a year.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex or plant plan discussed; technology spend is rising but no amount was disclosed and the brief says the AD-II licence is pending official announcement.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance was held, not raised, and the ₹500 crore PAT ambition has no disclosed FY27 support; H1 PAT of about ₹29 crore was partly a mix effect.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management's ₹2,500 crore AUM target by March 2027 needs about 42% growth in H2 from ₹1,766 crore, and gross NPA target below 1.50% is still 27 bps away from 1.77%; debt-to-equity at 2.89x against a lender limit of about 4x and pricing competition from about 50 replicators add risk.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Life insurance financing product expected live in about one month, and Arthum short-tenure products are launching now with monthly disbursements projected at ₹1,200-1,500 crore.

rows.label: Arthum contract-worker lending scale-up
rows.why: Management projects monthly disbursements of ₹1,200-1,500 crore, but the product is new, priced at 3-5% per month and not yet proven at scale.

rows.label: AD-II forex licence official announcement
rows.why: RBI approval is already granted and only the official announcement is pending, though the brief gives no date and the licence's business impact is not quantified.

rows.label: Equity needed beyond ₹3,000-3,500 crore AUM
rows.why: Current net worth of ₹604 crore plus accruals is expected to support borrowings for two years, so no fresh equity is needed before AUM reaches about ₹3,000-3,500 crore, likely in FY28.
